title: Tabal Kingdom
capsule: Tabal was a Luwian-speaking Neo-Hittite kingdom in southeastern Anatolia, occupying the plateau of modern Kayseri, Nevşehir, and Niğde provinces, bounded by the Halys (Kızılırmak) River to the north. Its rulers wrote in Hieroglyphic Luwian and maintained the political traditions of the collapsed Hittite empire; Tiglath-pileser III imposed tribute around 738 BCE and Sargon II married his daughter to king Ambaris around 721 BCE to secure loyalty. When Assyrian intelligence uncovered Ambaris's negotiations with Phrygia and Urartu, Sargon deported him in 713 BCE and annexed Tabal as a province; Sargon himself died fighting Cimmerians in or near Tabal in 705 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory is reasonably established from Assyrian annals and Luwian hieroglyphic monuments, but the shifting confederation of smaller client polities within the Tabal zone makes outer boundaries imprecise.
